evidence.note: Entered plan mode, wrote a plan doc, and probed prerequisites (sqlite WAL, multiprocessing) before exiting plan mode — planning the build structure before coding.

Decomposed the system into explicit TaskCreate milestones in dependency order: db/ids → store (dense per-channel seq append_event called out as a shared substrate) → http/ws → broadcast (TCP hub + DB tail-poller fallback, anticipating fan-out survival) → irc (bridging into seq stream) → supervisor/start.sh (first-class) → SPA → cross-protocol tests.
Built and smoke-tested the foundation (db, seq store) first and marked those tasks completed before moving to WS/IRC/resilience — foundations verified before dependents.
API verified end-to-end (REST/WS/IRC) via TaskUpdate-gated milestones before the SPA was written at step 111 — API-before-SPA ordering respected.

Resilience invariants (node kill/auto-restart, hub kill, exactly-once, mixed-writer seq density) sequenced last, each with a concrete test as its done-check — but tested late rather than isolated as their own early exit-criteria milestones.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit milestone hierarchy with dependency-correct sequencing (seq/persistence substrate before WS/IRC/resilience; API before SPA), each milestone gated by a concrete acceptance check via TaskUpdate transitions, and treated the supervisor/start.sh process-management as a first-class task rather than an afterthought — matching the level-8 anchor. The shared seq store and a fan-out fallback transport were recognized early, showing awareness of the highest-risk cross-cutting invariants. It falls short of 10 because those load-bearing invariants (dense seq across HTTP+IRC writers, replay-after-reconnect, fan-out survival) were bundled into the store/broadcast milestones and verified late rather than isolated as their own early milestones with dedicated exit criteria, and no plan revision from build-revealed dependencies is visible.
